summary.text: Kasie Whitener, a Libertarian business-school clinical assistant professor and former chair of the Libertarian Party of South Carolina, lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. Senate in South Carolina to Annie Andrews.
She teaches entrepreneurship and strategic management and is also a novelist.

paragraphs.text: Whitener was born in Florence, South Carolina, and graduated from Herndon High School.

She earned a bachelor's degree from Clemson University in 1999, a graduate degree from Winthrop University in 2004 and a Ph.D. from Capella University in 2014; her bachelor's and master's degrees are in English.
She has authored two novels, After December (2019) and Before Pittsburgh (2021), and served two terms as president of the South Carolina Writers Association, where she remains on the board.

Whitener works as a clinical assistant professor teaching entrepreneurship and strategic management and as a director of the Faber Entrepreneurship Center. She is also the voice of "Moore Impact," the Darla Moore School of Business's live radio show and podcast.
In the Libertarian Party, she served two terms as Richland County chairperson and then as chair of the state party.
She defeated Jason Brenkus at the Libertarian convention on April 11, 2026 to become the party's U.S. Senate nominee.
Whitener lives in Blythewood with her husband, Charlie, and their teenage daughter.
During the campaign, she promised to contain spending and demand fiscal responsibility, including a balanced budget delivered on time.
She received 1.2% of the vote to Annie Andrews's 51.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
